questions.q: A thin disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ has mass per unit area $\sigma\left(r\right) = kr^{2}$ where $r$ is the distance from its centre. Its moment inertia about an axis going through its centre of mass and perpendicular to its plane is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$dm = \sigma ⋅ dA = \sigma2\pirdr$
$= 2\pikr^{3}dr$
$M = ∫ dm = 2\pik\mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}r^{3}dr$
$= 2\pik\left(\dfrac{R^{4}}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\pikR^{4}}{2}$
$dI = dmr^{2} = 2\pikr^{5}dr$
$I = 2\pik\mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}r^{5}dr = 2\pik\dfrac{R6}{6} = \dfrac{2\pikR^{6}}{3 \times 2}$

since, $\text{M} = \dfrac{\pi kR4}{2}$

so,
$I = \dfrac{2MR^{2}}{3}$

questions.q:
A $\sqrt{34}m$ long ladder weighing $10$ kg leans on a frictionless wall. Its feet rest on the floor $3m$ away from the wall as shown in the figure. If ${F}_{f}$ and ${F}_{w}$ are the reaction forces of the floor and the wall, then ratio of $\dfrac{Fw}{Ff}$ will be :
(Use $g = 10ms^{- 2}$.)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying force balance in vertical direction

${N}_{1} = mg = 100N$

Applying torque balance at the bottom contact point,

$mg \times \dfrac{3}{2} = {N}_{2} \times 5 ⇒ {N}_{2} = {F}_{w} = 30N$

Applying force balance in horizontal direction

${f}_{s} = {N}_{2} = 30N$

Net reaction at the floor will be,

${F}_{f} = \sqrt{{N1}^{2} + {fs}^{2}} = \sqrt{{100}^{2} + {30}^{2}} = 10\sqrt{109}N$

Therefore,~$\dfrac{Fw}{Ff} = \dfrac{30}{10\sqrt{109}} = \dfrac{3}{109}$

questions.q: A mass $M$ hangs on a massless rod of length $l$ which rotates at a constant angular frequency. The mass $M$ moves with steady speed in a circular path of constant radius. Assume that the system is in steady circular motion with constant angular velocity $ω .$~The angular momentum of $M$ about point $A$ is ${L}_{A}$ which lies in the positive $z$ direction and the angular momentum of $M$ about $B$ is ${L}_{B} .$& The correct statement for this system is:
options: ${L}_{A}$ and ${L}_{B}$ are both constant in magnitude and direction
${L}_{B}$ is constant in direction with varying magnitude
${L}_{B}$ is constant, both in magnitude and direction
${L}_{A}$ is constant, both in magnitude and direction
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know,& $\overset{→}{L} = m ( \overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{v} )$

Now with respect to$A,$ we always get direction
of $\overset{→}{L}$ along $+ vez$-axis and also constant magnitude as mvr. But with respect to $B,$& we get constant magnitude but continuously changing direction.

questions.q: As shown in the figure, a bob of mass $m$ is tied to a massless string whose other end portion is wound on a fly wheel (disc) of radius $r$ and mass $m .$ When released from rest the bob starts falling vertically. When it has covered a distance of $h,$ the angular speed of the wheel will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using work-energy theorem&

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{Iω}^{2}$

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}{mω}^{2}r^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{mr2}{2}{ω}^{2}$~ ~ ( since~$I = \dfrac{mr2}{2}$~and~$v = r \omega$~)

$mgh = \dfrac{3}{4}{mω}^{2}r^{2}$

Hence,~$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3r^{2}}} = \dfrac{1}{r}\sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3}}$

questions.q: A cord of negligible mass is wound around the rim of a wheel supported by spokes with negligible mass. The mass of wheel is 10 kg and radius is 10 cm and it can freely rotate without any friction. Initially the wheel is at rest. If a steady pull of 20 N is applied on the cord, the angular velocity of the wheel, after the cord is unwound by 1 m , would be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{F}}=20 \times 1=20 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \therefore \quad \Delta \mathrm{KE}=20 \mathrm{~J}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{I} \omega^2 \\ & \mathrm{I}=\mathrm{MR}^2=10 \times 0.1^2=0.1 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^2 \\ & \therefore \quad 20=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.1 \times \omega^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \omega=20 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm\sec\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A heavy iron bar of weight $12$ kg is having its one end on the ground and the other on the shoulder of a man. The rod makes an angle $60 °$ with the horizontal, the normal force applied by the man on bar is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's consider the following diagram:

For the equilibrium of the system, the net torque, according to the above figure, on the system about point $A$ should be zero.

With reference to the above figure, the net anti-clockwise torque about $A$ is

${τ}_{a} = {F}_{2}L . . . \left(1\right)$

And, the net clockwise torque about the same point is

${τ}_{c} = Wcos\theta \times $\dfrac{L}{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

Equations (1) and (2) imply that

$Wcos\theta \times $\dfrac{L}{2} = {F}_{2}$L ⇒ 12 \times 10 \times cos60 ° \times \$left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right) = {F}_{2}$L ⇒ {F}_{2} = $\dfrac{120 \times 10 \times cos60 °}{2} =$30$

Hence, the required weight can be expressed as

${F}_{2} = 3kg - wt$

questions.q: Two identical spherical balls of mass $M$ and radius $R$ each are stuck on two ends of a rod of length $2R$ and mass $M$(see figure). The moment of inertia of the system about the axis passing perpendicularly through the centre of the rod is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying parallel axis theorem for the balls,
${I}_{b} = \left[\dfrac{2}{5}$MR^{2} + M \left($2R\right)2\right]$


${I}_{total} = 2{I}_{b} + {I}_{R}$
${I}_{total} = $\$left[\dfrac{2}{5}MR^{2} + $M\left($2R\right)2\right] \times2 + \dfrac{M}{12}\left(2R\right)2$

${I}_{total} = \dfrac{137}{15}MR^{2}$

$

questions.q: A uniform sphere of mass $500g$ rolls without slipping on a plane horizontal surface with its centre moving at a speed of $5.00cms^{- 1}$. Its kinetic energy is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$K . E$ of the sphere $=$ Translational $K . E +$ Rotational $K . E$
$= \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{K2}{R2}\right), K =$ Radius of gyration
$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{2}{100}\right)2 \left($1 + $\dfrac{2}{5}\right)
$= $\dfrac{35}{4} \times {10}^{- 4}$J$
$= 8.75 $\times {10}^{- 4}$J$
$

questions.q: A solid sphere is rolling without slipping on a horizontal plane. The ratio of the linear kinetic energy of the centre of mass of the sphere and rotational kinetic energy is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{KE}_{(T)}=\frac{1}{2} m v^2 \\
& \mathrm{KE}_{(R)}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{5} m R^2 \cdot \frac{v^2}{R^2}=\frac{1}{2} m v^2\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)
\end{aligned}$
So, $\frac{\mathrm{KE}_{(T)}}{\mathrm{KE}_{(R)}}=\frac{5}{2}$

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II

List-I List-II
(A) Moment of inertia of solid sphere
of radius $R$ about any tangent.		 (I) $\dfrac{5}{3}{MR}^{2}$
(B) Moment of inertia of hollow sphere of radius
\left(R\right)$ about any tangent.		 (II) $\dfrac{7}{5}{MR}^{2}$
(C) Moment of inertia of circular ring of radius
\left(R\right)$ about its diameter.		 (III) $\dfrac{1}{4}{MR}^{2}$
(D) Moment of inertia of circular disc of radius
\left(R\right)$ about any diameter.		 (IV) $\dfrac{1}{2}{MR}^{2}$
$
options: $A - II, B - I, C - IV, D - III$
$A - I, B - II, C - IV, D - III$
$A - II, B - I, C - III, D - IV$
$A - I, B - II, C - III, D - IV$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For solid sphere

${I}_{0} = {I}_{com} + MR^{2}$~ (Using parallel axis theorem)

${I}_{0} = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^{2} + MR^{2}$

${I}_{0} = \dfrac{7}{5}MR^{2}⇒ A \to II$

For hollow sphere

$I = {I}_{com} + MR^{2} ⇒ I = \dfrac{5}{3}MR^{2} ⇒ B \to I$

For Circular ring

${I}_{1} + {I}_{2} = {I}_{3}$ ( Using perpendicular axis theorem)

By symmetry MOI

About $1$ and $2$ Axis are same i.e.

${I}_{1} = {I}_{2}$

$∴ 2{I}_{1} = {I}_{3} = MR^{2} \left(∵ {I}_{com} = MR^{2}\right)$

${I}_{1} = $\dfrac{MR^{2}}{2}$⇒ C \to IV$

Similarly in disc

$2{I}_{1} = $\dfrac{MR^{2}}{2} \left$\{∵ {I}_{com} = \dfrac{MR^{2}}{2}\right\}$

${I}_{1} = \dfrac{MR^{2}}{4}⇒ D \to III

$

questions.q: A metal coin of mass $5g$ and radius $1$ cm is fixed to a thin stick $AB$ of negligible mass as shown in the figure. The system is initially at rest. The constant torque, that will make the system rotate about $AB$ at $25$ rotations per second in $5s$ , is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As torque $τ$ is constant.
$\omega = \dfrac{τ}{I}t$
$τ = \dfrac{\omegaI}{t} = \dfrac{\left(2\pin\right) \times \dfrac{5}{4}mr^{2}}{t}$
$= \dfrac{\left(2\pi \times 25\right) \times \dfrac{5}{4} \times 5 \times {10}^{- 3} \times {\left(1 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}^{2}}{5}$
$= 196 \times {10}^{- 7}$
$\approx 2 ⋅ 0 \times {10}^{- 5}Nm$

questions.q: Angular momentum of a single particle moving with constant speed along circular path :
options: remains same in magnitude but changes in the direction
remains same in magnitude and direction
changes in magnitude but remains same in the direction
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The angular momentum is defined as the vector product of linear momentum and perpendicular distance,& $\overset{→}{L} = \overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{p} = \overset{→}{r} \times m\overset{→}{v}$,& And direction will be upward & remain constant.

questions.q: The following bodies are made to roll up (without slipping) the same inclined plane from a horizontal plane: (i) a ring of radius $R,$ (ii) a solid cylinder of radius $\dfrac{R}{2}$ and (iii) a solid sphere of radius $\dfrac{R}{4} .$ If, in each case, the speed of the center of mass at the bottom of the incline is same, the ratio of the maximum heights they climb is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From conservation of mechanical energy.
\left(\dfrac{1}{2}{m}_{R}v^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{R}{\omega}_r^{2}\right) = {m}_{R}g{h}_{R} ⇒ \dfrac{V^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{V^{2}}{2} = g{h}_{R}$
\left(\dfrac{1}{2}{m}_{d}v^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{d}{\omega}_d^{2}\right) = {m}_{d}g{h}_{d} ⇒ \dfrac{V^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{V^{2}}{4} = g{h}_{d}$
\left(\dfrac{1}{2}{m}_{s}v^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{s}{\omega}_s^{2}\right) = {m}_{s}g{h}_{s} ⇒ \dfrac{V^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{V^{2}}{5} = g{h}_{s}$
$∴ {h}_{R}: {h}_{d}: {h}_{s} = 1: \dfrac{3}{4}: \dfrac{7}{10} = 20: 15: 14

questions.q: For a uniform rectangular sheet shown in the figure, the ratio of moments of inertia about the axes perpendicular to the sheet and passing through& $O$~(the centre of mass) and $O$' (corner point) is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We will use Parallel Axes Theorem here,

Distance between& $OO^{'}$~is,

$OO^{'} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{a2}{4} + \dfrac{b2}{4}}$

So, according to parallel axis theorem we have,

$\dfrac{IO}{IO^{'}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{M}{12}\left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right)}{\dfrac{M}{12}\left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right) + M\left(\dfrac{a2}{4} + \dfrac{b2}{4}\right)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{M}{12}\left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right)}{\dfrac{M}{3}\left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{4}$&

The difference in the height,~$h \left(incm\right)& of liquid at the Centre of vessel and at the sides of the vessel will be :

questions.subject: Physics

ρ\left($dr\right){#969;}^{2}r = ρg\left($dh\right)

questions.q: If force $\overset{→}{F} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ acts on a particle having position vector $2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ then, the torque about the origin will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Torque in vector form is expressed as vector multiplication of position vector and force.

$\overset{→}{τ} = \overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{F}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{τ} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & - 2\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{τ} = \left(- 2 - 8\right)\overset{^}{i} - \left(- 4 - 6\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(8 - 3\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{τ} = \left(- 10\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right)Nm$

questions.q: A solid sphere and a hollow sphere of the same mass and of same radius are rolled on an inclined plane. Let the time taken to reach the bottom by the solid sphere and the hollow sphere be $t_1$ and $t_2$, respectively, then
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}}}} \\ & \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}{1+\frac{\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{cm}}}{\mathrm{MR}^2}} \\ & \mathrm{a}_1=\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}_1}=\frac{5 \mathrm{~g} \sin \theta}{7} \ldots . . \text { Solid } \\ & \mathrm{a}_2=\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}_2}=\frac{3 \mathrm{~g} \sin \theta}{5} \ldots . . \text { Hollow } \\ & \mathrm{a}_1 \gt \mathrm{a}_2 \\ & \mathrm{t}_1 \lt \mathrm{t}_2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Solid sphere $A$ is rotating about an axis $PQ$. If the radius of the sphere is $5$ cm, then its radius of gyration about $PQ$ will be $\sqrt{x}cm$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using parallel axis theorem,

${I}_{PQ} = {I}_{COM } + Md^{2}$

$= \dfrac{2}{5}MR^{2} + Md^{2}$

$= M \left[\dfrac{2}{5} \times {5}^{2} + {10}^{2}\right]

$= M [ 110 ] = Mk^{2}$

$⇒ k = $\sqrt{110}$cm$

Therefore,~$x = 110$.

$

questions.q: A solid disc of radius $20$ cm and mass $10$ kg is rotating with an angular velocity of $600$ rpm, about an axis normal to its circular plane and passing through its centre of mass. The retarding torque required to bring the disc at rest in $10s$ is _________\pi \times {10}^{- 1}Nm
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$τ = \dfrac{\Delta L}{\Deltat} = \dfrac{I\left({ω}_{f} - {ω}_{i}\right)}{\Deltat}$

$τ = \dfrac{\dfrac{mR^{2}}{2} \times [ 0 - \omega ]}{\Deltat}$

$= \dfrac{10 \times \left(20 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)2}{2} \times \dfrac{600 \times \pi}{30 \times 10}$

$= 0 . 4\pi = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 1}$

questions.q: A body of mass $m$ is projected with a speed $u$ making an angle of ${45}^{o}$ with the ground. The angular momentum of the body about the point of projection, at the highest point is expressed as $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}mu^{3}}{Xg}$. The value of $X$ is_______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Consider projection as shown in above diagram.

At the topmost point, velocity of the body will be $ucos45 °$.

Therefore, we can write the required angular momentum as

$L = \left(m{u}_{H}\right)\timesH = \lleft(mucos\theta\right)\left(\dfrac{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}\right)

$= mu^{3} $\times \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}g}$⇒ X = 8$

$

questions.q: A disc of mass $1$ kg and radius $R$ is free of rotate about a horizontal axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to the plane of disc. A body of same mass as that of disc is fixed at the highest point of the disc. Now the system is released, when the body comes to the lowest position, its angular speed will be $4\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{3R}}rads^{- 1}$ where $x =$& _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the angular speed of disc be& $\omega$.

Using conservation of mechanical energy

$mg2R = \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{disc}{ω}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{particle}{ω}^{2}$

Where,~$I$~is moment of inertia.

$⇒ mg2R = \dfrac{\omega2}{2} \left[\dfrac{m2}{2} +mR^{2}\right]$

$⇒ mg2R = \dfrac{\omega2}{2} \left(\dfrac{3}{2}mR^{2}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{4}{ω}^{2} = \dfrac{2g}{R}$~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ &

& $⇒ {ω}^{2} = \dfrac{8g}{3R}$

Thus, angular speed is~$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{80}{3R}}rads^{- 1}$

Given~$\omega = 4\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{3R}}$

Comparing both,~$16\dfrac{x}{3R} = \dfrac{80}{3R}$

Therefore, the value of~$x = 5$.

questions.q: A circular ring and a solid sphere having same radius roll down on an inclined plane from rest without slipping. The ratio of their velocities when reached at the bottom of the plane is $\sqrt{\frac{x}{5}}$ where $\mathrm{x}=$ _____
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying Mechanical Energy conservation :
$\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}+\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{f}}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 0+\mathrm{Mgh}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2\left(1+\frac{\mathrm{k}^2}{\mathrm{R}^2}\right)+0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~V}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{gh}}{1+\frac{\mathrm{k}^2}{\mathrm{R}^2}}}
\end{aligned}$
So Ratio of velocities
$\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\text {Ring }}}{\mathrm{V}_{\text {solids sphere }}}=\sqrt{\frac{1+\frac{2}{5}}{1+1}}=\sqrt{\frac{7}{10}}$
$\mathrm{x}=3.5$ Rounding off $\mathrm{x}=4$
